title: Swift: portable language foundations and Apple app architecture
summary: 48 detailed lessons from first programs through language mechanisms, reliable systems and independently designed projects.

lessons.title: A Swift source file and its explicit entrypoint
lessons.outcome: Compile and run a Swift program with an explicit @main entry point and check a computed value with precondition.
lessons.lab: Compute the capacity of three shelves holding eight books each.
lessons.verification: Three shelves of eight books hold 24 books.

lessons.title: Constants, variables and static types
lessons.outcome: Use let and var deliberately and convert between numeric types explicitly.
lessons.lab: Compute a mean from an integer total and count using a deliberate conversion.
lessons.verification: The mean is 3.5, while integer division of the same values would give 3.

lessons.title: Numeric limits and intentional arithmetic
lessons.outcome: Detect integer overflow with reporting arithmetic and use Decimal where exact decimal values matter.
lessons.lab: Write checked quantity addition that returns an explicit rejected outcome.
lessons.verification: 200 + 50 is accepted as 250; 200 + 56 is rejected instead of wrapping to 0.

lessons.title: Strings, Unicode and collection indices
lessons.outcome: Count and slice strings by Character and index, not by assumed byte or code unit positions.
lessons.lab: Write a function returning the first Character as an optional value.
lessons.verification: The first Character of 😀B is 😀, and empty text gives nil.

lessons.title: Optionals and honest absence
lessons.outcome: Represent absence with optionals and unwrap them safely without inventing sentinel values.
lessons.lab: Write a parser accepting only present nonnegative integers.
lessons.verification: 12 and 0 are accepted; nil, -3 and x are rejected.

lessons.title: Branches, switch and exhaustive reasoning
lessons.outcome: Write exhaustive switch statements and guards that cover every case, including boundaries.
lessons.lab: Write a three-way classifier for negative, zero and positive quantities.
lessons.verification: -2, 0 and 7 are classified as negative, zero and positive.

lessons.title: Loops, invariants and safe traversal
lessons.outcome: Write loops with safe traversal and report not-found with an optional result.
lessons.lab: Implement a first-match search with an optional result.
lessons.verification: The first 7 is at offset 1; a missing target and an empty array give nil.

lessons.title: Functions, argument labels and value contracts
lessons.outcome: Write functions with clear argument labels and choose between value parameters and inout.
lessons.lab: Write a pure function normalizing a quantity without mutating its caller.
lessons.verification: 15 is normalized to 10 and -4 to 0, while the caller's value stays 15.

lessons.title: Arrays and copy-on-write value semantics
lessons.outcome: Predict copy-on-write behavior of arrays and transform them without changing the source.
lessons.lab: Build a filtered array without changing the source.
lessons.verification: The filtered array is [2, 4] and the source is unchanged.

lessons.title: Dictionaries, sets and stable hashing
lessons.outcome: Use dictionaries and sets for lookup and deduplication and sort them for stable output.
lessons.lab: Build a unique sorted list of accepted inventory names.
lessons.verification: The accepted names are apple, fig and pear, each once and sorted.

lessons.title: Tuples, enums and associated values
lessons.outcome: Model alternatives with enums and associated values handled by exhaustive switches.
lessons.lab: Model loading, ready and failed states with an enum.
lessons.verification: The states render as loading, ready:3 and failed:offline.

lessons.title: Structures and controlled value mutation
lessons.outcome: Encapsulate state in structs with private(set) and mutating methods that keep invariants.
lessons.lab: Build a bounded counter with private mutation.
lessons.verification: Two increments succeed, the third is refused, and the value stays at 2.

lessons.title: Classes, identity and shared state
lessons.outcome: Choose classes for shared identity and structs for values, and predict sharing and copying.
lessons.lab: Choose class or struct for a shared connection coordinator and a coordinate value.
lessons.verification: Both coordinator references see 1 open connection, while moving the copied coordinate leaves the original at x = 1.

lessons.title: Properties, observers and derived state
lessons.outcome: Derive computed properties from one stored source of truth and use observers deliberately.
lessons.lab: Build a value model with one stored unit and a documented converted view.
lessons.verification: 3.048 meters reads as 10 feet.

lessons.title: Closures, captures and transformation pipelines
lessons.outcome: Write closures, control what they capture and compose transformation pipelines.
lessons.lab: Write a function accepting a transformation closure.
lessons.verification: Applying the closure gives 10, 20 and 30.

lessons.title: Foundation project: an honest inventory importer
lessons.outcome: Build an honest inventory importer that reports sorted totals and rejected lines.
lessons.lab: Produce a sorted text report with accepted totals and rejected count.
lessons.verification: The report lists apple: 3, pear: 3 and rejected: 1.

lessons.title: Protocols and behavioral substitution
lessons.outcome: Program against protocols so implementations can be substituted without changing callers.
lessons.lab: Define a protocol for a deterministic label formatter.
lessons.verification: The formatter produces 1 item and 3 items, identically on every call.

lessons.title: Generics and relationships between types
lessons.outcome: Write generic types and functions with the constraints their operations need.
lessons.lab: Create a generic immutable triple with a rotation operation.
lessons.verification: Rotating (1, 2, 3) gives (2, 3, 1).

lessons.title: Associated types, opaque results and existentials
lessons.outcome: Use associated types, opaque results and existentials and explain what each hides.
lessons.lab: Write a generic transformation preserving the producer item type.
lessons.verification: Transforming the produced 7 gives 8, still an Int.

lessons.title: Collection protocols, laziness and algorithm costs
lessons.outcome: Work with collection protocols, slices and lazy sequences and reason about their cost.
lessons.lab: Write a generic sum over Sequence where the element type is suitable.
lessons.verification: The sum works for Ints (6) and Doubles (4.0) and returns 0 for an empty sequence.

lessons.title: Throwing functions and explicit result values
lessons.outcome: Throw and handle typed errors and convert between throwing calls and Result values.
lessons.lab: Write a throwing validator for an inventory record.
lessons.verification: A valid record passes; an empty name throws RecordError.emptyName.

lessons.title: ARC, weak references and retain cycles
lessons.outcome: Prevent retain cycles with weak and unowned references and verify that objects are released.
lessons.lab: Design a weak delegate relationship.
lessons.verification: The listener receives finished; after it is released the weak delegate becomes nil and finish() does nothing.

lessons.title: Codable and validated data boundaries
lessons.outcome: Encode and decode with Codable and validate decoded values before trusting them.
lessons.lab: Write a decoder that validates before returning a trusted item.
lessons.verification: The valid item is returned; quantity -1 decodes but is rejected before it is trusted.

lessons.title: Files, URLs and owned persistence
lessons.outcome: Persist data in owned temporary files with Foundation URLs and remove them on every path.
lessons.lab: Persist a Codable value in a temporary file and validate after reading.
lessons.verification: The value read back equals the saved one and passes the quantity check; the folder is removed at the end of the block.

lessons.title: Dates, calendars and elapsed time
lessons.outcome: Handle dates, calendars and elapsed time with fixed fixtures independent of the time zone.
lessons.lab: Build a report from fixed timestamp fixtures.
lessons.verification: The report reads 165 minutes from 2025-03-01T22:30:00Z.

lessons.title: Swift packages and module boundaries
lessons.outcome: Build and run a Swift package and explain its module and target boundaries.
lessons.lab: Reproduce Example A (Keep a pure core function) and Example B (Separate presentation from calculation) and explain each check.
lessons.verification: The pure kernel is suitable for a reusable library. Presentation is independently testable.

lessons.title: Testing behavior with the prepared package
lessons.outcome: Write behavior tests for the prepared package with XCTest and know where Swift Testing fits.
lessons.lab: Reproduce Example A (Check independently derived cases) and Example B (Catch a plausible wrong boundary) and explain each check.
lessons.verification: Normal and boundary values satisfy the clamp contract. The zero case catches the wrong default and clamping is idempotent.

lessons.title: Async functions and suspension points
lessons.outcome: Write async functions and explain where suspension points occur.
lessons.lab: Write an async adapter that returns a validated domain value.
lessons.verification: The adapter awaits the raw text and returns Quantity(value: 12).

lessons.title: Task groups and bounded parallel ownership
lessons.outcome: Run bounded parallel work with task groups that own their child tasks.
lessons.lab: Implement bounded admission for a small list with at most two outstanding children.
lessons.verification: All five inputs are processed, and at most two child tasks were ever outstanding.

lessons.title: Cancellation and cleanup in asynchronous work
lessons.outcome: Cancel asynchronous work cooperatively and clean up on every exit path.
lessons.lab: Write a bounded processing loop with cleanup on cancellation.
lessons.verification: When cancellation is observed before the fourth item, items 1 to 3 are done and cleanup still runs; an uncancelled task finishes both items.

lessons.title: Actors and serialized state ownership
lessons.outcome: Protect mutable state with actors so access is serialized by construction.
lessons.lab: Implement a bounded actor-owned queue with explicit admission.
lessons.verification: Two offers are admitted, the third is refused, and the first item taken is 1.

lessons.title: Composition project: an actor-owned import ledger
lessons.outcome: Build an actor-owned import ledger with idempotent operations and conflict detection.
lessons.lab: Add a read-only receipt lookup that never re-executes work.
lessons.verification: The lookup finds receipt 3 for one, reports nil for two, and the work ran only once.

lessons.title: Sendable and strict concurrency boundaries
lessons.outcome: Pass only Sendable values across concurrency boundaries under Swift 6 strict checking.
lessons.lab: Replace a shared mutable result class with a sendable value result.
lessons.verification: The task returns Summary(count: 3, total: 9).

lessons.title: AsyncSequence, streams and bounded buffering
lessons.outcome: Produce and consume AsyncStreams with explicit completion and bounded buffering.
lessons.lab: Build a finite event stream with explicit completion ownership.
lessons.verification: The consumer receives start, progress and done, and its loop ends.

lessons.title: Unsafe memory, buffers and scope-limited access
lessons.outcome: Keep unsafe buffer access scoped and hidden behind a safe function contract.
lessons.lab: Wrap a scoped read-only buffer operation behind a safe function contract.
lessons.verification: The safe wrapper returns 9 for [2, 3, 4] and 0 for an empty array.

lessons.title: Performance, copy costs and complexity
lessons.outcome: Compare algorithm costs and copy behavior with evidence rather than assumptions.
lessons.lab: Compare repeated array scans with one built Set under the same identity policy.
lessons.verification: Both approaches find 2 of the 3 queries.

lessons.title: Property wrappers and reusable access policy
lessons.outcome: Write property wrappers that apply one reusable access or normalization policy.
lessons.lab: Create a wrapper with an explicit normalization policy for a local display field.
lessons.verification: Both assignment and initialization store the trimmed text Report and x.

lessons.title: Result builders and declarative composition
lessons.outcome: Compose declarative structures with result builders, including optional parts.
lessons.lab: Build a small report declaration using the existing builder.
lessons.verification: The report contains Summary and Totals; the Warnings section is omitted.

lessons.title: App architecture: a portable domain core
lessons.outcome: Separate a portable domain core from the Apple app and test it on its own.
lessons.lab: Reproduce Example A (Apply a domain action) and Example B (Keep identity stable during edits) and explain each check.
lessons.verification: The transformed item changes completion while retaining the original value. Completion changes do not manufacture a new identity.

lessons.title: SwiftUI state, bindings and a single source of truth
lessons.outcome: Manage SwiftUI state and bindings with a single source of truth.
lessons.lab: Reproduce Example A (Derive presentation from one state) and Example B (A state change updates its derived view) and explain each check.
lessons.verification: The label follows the stored completion state. Changing completion changes the derived label while retaining the title.

lessons.title: Navigation, stable identity and deep-link validation
lessons.outcome: Navigate by stable identity and validate deep links before acting on them.
lessons.lab: Reproduce Example A (Parse an admitted route) and Example B (Reject unrelated or incomplete links) and explain each check.
lessons.verification: The admitted scheme and host resolve to item one. Unrelated schemes, missing identity and unlisted actions are rejected.

lessons.title: App persistence, migrations and recoverable saves
lessons.outcome: Save, load and migrate app data with recoverable errors.
lessons.lab: Reproduce Example A (Read the supported version) and Example B (Refuse an unknown future schema) and explain each check.
lessons.verification: The supported envelope round-trips with two titles. The unsupported document is rejected without modifying its payload.

lessons.title: Networking, loading states and stale-result protection
lessons.outcome: Model loading states and discard stale network results with a deterministic fake transport.
lessons.lab: Reproduce Example A (Accept the current request result) and Example B (Ignore a superseded result) and explain each check.
lessons.verification: The matching generation updates current state. The stale response cannot overwrite the newer value.

lessons.title: Accessibility, localization and inclusive interaction
lessons.outcome: Make an app accessible and localizable with meaningful labels and stable identity.
lessons.lab: Reproduce Example A (Describe state with words) and Example B (Keep identity separate from translation) and explain each check.
lessons.verification: The label communicates completion without relying on color. Switching language changes the title from Read to Lire while the completion saved under lesson-one still shows complete.

lessons.title: UIKit and AppKit integration boundaries
lessons.outcome: Wrap UIKit and AppKit views at clear integration boundaries.
lessons.lab: Reproduce Example A (Avoid redundant imperative updates) and Example B (Retain user changes as actions) and explain each check.
lessons.verification: The same value is not assigned twice. The portable kernel exposes a deliberate state transition.

lessons.title: App tests, simulator evidence and signing
lessons.outcome: Run app tests on simulators or macOS destinations and explain signing requirements.
lessons.lab: Reproduce Example A (Separate acceptance categories) and Example B (Require every declared release gate) and explain each check.
lessons.verification: Domain and package evidence do not imply UI or device qualification. Save/reload remains an explicit incomplete gate.

lessons.title: Multiplatform design and deployment contracts
lessons.outcome: Separate portable and platform-specific code and state each platform's deployment contract.
lessons.lab: Reproduce Example A (Keep portable policy independent) and Example B (Declare a capability rather than guess) and explain each check.
lessons.verification: The same domain summary works without a UI framework. The Linux capability set does not invent SwiftUI support.

lessons.title: Capstone: an offline-first study planner
lessons.outcome: Build and test a complete offline-first study planner across the portable core and the Apple app.
lessons.lab: Reproduce Example A (Produce a stable completion summary) and Example B (Preserve identity across a value update) and explain each check.
lessons.verification: One of two uniquely identified items is complete. The update retains identity and the prior snapshot.
